content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The author proposed RephraseTTS for the task of text-conditioned speech insertion. The RephraseTTS model follows a transformer-based non-autoregressive architecture that allows speech insertions of variable lengths, which are dynamically determined during inference based on the text transcript and available partial input. Generated speech samples show that RephraseTTS can maintain the speaker’s identity, prosody and other spectral properties of the available speech input and outperforms the existing adaptive text to speech baselines.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
It seems like the author only tested the model and provided speech samples with the to-be-inserted text same as the ground truth text (maybe to make it comparable with the ground truth speech). If this is the case, using different from ground truth text may hurt the model performance significantly, since RephraseTTS simply keeps the to-be-inserted part of generated speech segment and stitches it with the ground-truth audio of the available part, and concatenation method empirically couldn't generate speech with good smoothness.

In section 2, the author argued that "Our method directly outputs a high quality speech output with dynamic length test and does not require a second stage of enhancement.", compared to other method which "uses the second stage to increase the quality of the reconstructed speech introduced by mean-square-error loss used during first stage of the training." In section 3.3.4, however, the author said "We train our RephraseTTS model in two phases. In the first phase, we only train with the L1 reconstruction loss ... In the second phase, we also add the adversarial LSGAN ... to our main objective.", which seems inconsistent with the previous statement.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper needs further polishing before publication.
1. Some important implementation details and ablation study are put into appendices. 
2. The mean opinion score (MOS) doesn't have confidence interval reported.
3. Typos: (i) in section 2: "Text-based speech insertion." -> "Text-based Speech Insertion." (ii) in section 4: please use period and bold type consistently in headings.
content.summary_of_the_review: The ratings are given based on the author's statements, reported results and provided demos.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper aims at the text-conditioned speech insertion task, inserting a speech sample in an input speech sample, conditioned on the corresponding complete text transcript. 

This paper proposes a deep neural network for dynamic length speech insertion using cross-modal attention with adversarial local, global, and style losses.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength 
1. It performs better than state-of-the-art methods adaptive TTS methods in the quantitive result.
2. The cross-modal attention encodes multimodal information and works well.
3. The method is capable of maintaining the speaker characteristics in the generated parts of the speech, and the subjectively human participants also favour the output of the proposed network.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
This paper is clearly written, but not novel enough. 

Cross attention mechanism is not a brand-new invention, it first appeared in the original Transformer paper, used to connect the encoder and decoder, your CROSS-MODAL ATTENTION seems nothing different. 

The ablation experiment of adversarial local, global, and style losses demonstrated that they make the quantitative metric MCD better, but I can't hear the difference in the audio clip proved in Supplementary Material.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper is not novel enough, and there is merely a weak improvement in the generated voice clip.

content.confidence: 2: You are willing to defend your assessment, but it is quite likely that you did not understand the central parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a model that performs text based speech insertion with variable duration. IT takes the masked input and the phonemic representation of the full text and encode them separately using neural encoders and then applies multiple-head cross-modal attention. Using a variance adapter, it generates an encoding of the masked region which is then inserted into the input spectrogram. To train the model, a weighted combination of various losses have been used which includes an L1 reconstruction loss, LS-GAN-style loss terms with feature matching loss, and a style matching loss. The style matching loss is trained using a separate small network and its loss is based on triplet loss. Experiments on LibriTTS show that the proposed method achieves higher MOS than Meta-StyleSpeech but still far from reaching the quality of a re-synthesis of the ground truth audio. Objective mel-cepstral distortion loss also supports the same conclusion.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- The variance adaptor allows the model to generate variable length outputs for the missing segments which is usually not possible in earlier speech inpainting systems.
- The model performs well as compared to a relatively strong baseline (Meta-StyleSpeech).


Weaknesses: 
- The paper might have been better organized. Background section and the losses occupy relatively a large space leaving the experimental results to the appendix. At least, it could have been better to include the ablation study in the main text.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: It is clearly written but the relatively long background sections have left little space for experimental discussions. Minor comment: Please write eq. as Eq. For example in Section 3.3. 

Quality: Even though the paper proposes some ways of inserting speech, the findings are relatively less interesting because we usually expect the re-synthesis of the original signal to be of higher perceptual quality as compared to the synthesized versions. The paper mainly shows another method to slightly close the performance gap between synthetic and real audio. 
Some questions: 
1. Fig. 2, Lower left figure, why do not we have a green arrow between $R_1$ and $F_1$? 
2. In the LS-GAN formulation of the additional loss terms, is it sufficient to add the losses together? Would it be better if the generator and discriminator loss are trained separately? 

Novelty: 
Might be limited but sufficient. Most of the subcomponents build upon FastSpeech2 model. The main addition here is the addition of a speech branch and a cross-modal attention module to combine audio and text information. 

Reproducibility: It should probably be reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper adds speech input into the FastSpeech2 model using a cross-attention module and tries to achieve text based speech insertion with a variable duration. Subjective and objective evaluations of the synthesized audio show that the proposed approach outperform Meta-StyleSpeech and also that synthetic audio quality is still far from real audio especially when the audio is longer. The paper is clearly written but could be organized in a better way so that it can include some of the experiments in the main paper instead of the appendix.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a text-conditioned speech insertion method, RephaseTTS. RephraseTTS computes the speech representation for insertion from the reference speech by using cross-modal attention between text and speech representations. This work uses some additional loss for speech characteristics. The experimental results show that RephraseTTS outperforms Meta-StyleSpeech.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths 
- RephraseTTS outperforms the adaptive TTS baseline (MetaStyleSpeech) on LibriTTS dataset.
- This paper shows the ablation study on each loss and cross-attention module. 
- All the details of each module and experiment are well explained. 

 Weaknesses
* The paper lacks experimental results and analysis, and Section 3 is lengthy. Some subsections are directly adapted from the previous work (FastSpeech 2) and well-known techniques. It is necessary to reduce the content of Section 3 and add more results and analysis.
* Not enough baselines for model comparison. In table 1, the paper compares the proposed method only with MSS. MSS can perform text-based insertion, but it was originally proposed for adaptive TTS. (Recommend to compare with not only adaptive TTS baselines but also other text-based speech insertion models.)
* In Table 1, only the averaged values of the MOS are provided. For the reliability of the comparison, a 95% confidence interval is required.
* Insufficient evaluation metrics. This paper only shows the evaluation metrics for naturalness. However, since the text-based speech insertion task has to maintain the speaker’s voice characteristics, and prosody, the paper has to evaluate other aspects of speech such as speaker similarity between X^I and [X^B, X^A].
- Lack of analysis. Since RephaseTTS uses the cross-attention to the reference speech, it might highly depend on the duration of the reference speech and the length of the insertion. However, the paper does not have any analysis of these factors. If the duration of the reference speech is too short or the length of the insertion is too long, the performance of RephraseTTS can degrade a lot. (ex. the reference speech: Thanks → want to generate: Thank you very much) 
- From the point of view of TTS models, dynamic length insertion does not appear to be a significant contribution.

Minor typos
* In Section 3.2.4, (X^B, X^B), (X^B, Z^I, X^B) → (X^B, X^A), (X^B, Z^I, X^A)
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper explains the proposed method in detail. Table 1 has to be modified with more baselines and 95% CI. The paper needs to add more analysis of the proposed method.
content.summary_of_the_review: This task proposes the model for the text-based speech insertion task, which is a relatively narrow task in TTS. In order to fit into the ICLR, it is necessary to show a wider range of applicable situations and motivations for the task. If not, the paper is more suitable for speech conferences.
